name: Digital Literacy Classes and Tech Help
description: Free beginner classes and one-on-one tech help at San Francisco Public Library branches. Learn to use a computer, email, the internet, online forms, smartphones and video calls at your own pace. Good first step for people with little or no computer experience, with some help offered in Spanish and Chinese.
verify_note: Confirm current class calendar, branch and language availability with SFPL.

name: Digital Skills Classes in Your Language
description: Free small-group digital literacy classes taught by volunteers, often in the learner's own language, including Spanish, Cantonese, Vietnamese and Tagalog. Covers computer basics, internet safety, email, and online job applications. Designed for adults who are new to computers and want confidence before a career program.
verify_note: Confirm class sites, schedule and languages offered with CTN.

name: Noncredit Computer Basics and Office Skills
description: Tuition-free noncredit computer classes at City College of San Francisco covering keyboarding, Windows, Microsoft Word, Excel and Google tools. Evening and weekend sections at neighborhood centers make it workable for people with daytime jobs. A gentle on-ramp to IT and office careers.
neighborhood: Mission (Mission Center) and other CCSF centers
verify_note: Noncredit courses are generally free; confirm current sections, centers and schedule with CCSF.

name: Digital Skills and Job Readiness
description: Free digital skills and job readiness support: computer basics, resume writing, online job search and interview practice, with career coaching. Helpful for people returning to work or changing careers who want practical skills and a coach.
verify_note: Confirm current program offerings, location and schedule with Goodwill SF Bay.

name: Job Readiness and Intro to Coding
description: Free job readiness program and introductory coding classes based in the Tenderloin. Covers professional skills, resume and interview prep, and beginner web development, with connections to employers. Built for people facing barriers to employment, including people who were formerly incarcerated or unhoused.
verify_note: Confirm cohort dates, schedule and eligibility with Code Tenderloin.

name: IT Support (CompTIA A+ prep)
description: Tuition-free, full-time IT support training that prepares learners for the CompTIA A+ certification and entry-level help desk and desktop support jobs. Runs roughly 12 to 16 weeks at about 40 hours per week during the day, with career coaching and employer connections. No stipend is paid, so learners need a way to cover living costs while training.
requirements: Provider sets eligibility, including work authorization
verify_note: Free and no stipend per the design doc; confirm campus, cohort dates and course length with Per Scholas.

name: TechSF IT Help Desk Training
description: No-cost TechSF tech training through JVS for San Francisco job seekers, preparing for IT help desk and technical support roles with job placement support. Offered at no cost to participants. Some TechSF programs require work authorization and other documents, which the provider checks.
requirements: Provider sets eligibility, which may include work authorization and SF residency documents
verify_note: Free per the design doc; confirm schedule, hours and eligibility documents with JVS.

name: Computer Technician / IT Support Certificate (evening)
provider: City College of San Francisco (Free City College)
description: Credit certificate in computer networking and IT support at City College of San Francisco, with evening sections that fit around a daytime job. Free City College covers enrollment fees for eligible San Francisco residents, so tuition is typically free; learners pay for books, a laptop, and certification exams such as CompTIA A+. Two semesters part-time.
requirements: Free City College eligibility set by CCSF (SF residency)
verify_note: Confirm the certificate name, evening sections and Free City College eligibility with CCSF; books estimate is a planning assumption.

name: Google IT Support Professional Certificate
description: Self-paced online IT support certificate covering troubleshooting, networking, operating systems, system administration and security. Study evenings or weekends from a laptop. Paid by monthly subscription; about six months at 10 hours per week.
verify_note: Cost assumes about $49 per month for six months; confirm current price and any free access through libraries or scholarships.

name: Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate
description: Self-paced online certificate in data analytics: spreadsheets, SQL, data cleaning, dashboards and presenting findings. Good for people who like numbers and want office or digital roles in any industry. Paid by monthly subscription; about six months at 10 hours per week.
verify_note: Cost assumes about $49 per month for six months; confirm current price and any free access.

name: CompTIA A+ Certification Exams (Core 1 and Core 2)
description: The industry-recognized entry-level IT certification employers ask for in help desk and desktop support jobs. Requires passing two exams, Core 1 and Core 2, taken at a testing center or online. Pairs with any IT support training program.
verify_note: Exam fee is an estimate of two vouchers at about $265 each; confirm current CompTIA pricing and any discounted vouchers through the training provider.

name: Year Up Bay Area: IT and Business Operations
description: Full-time, tuition-free training for young adults followed by an internship at a corporate partner, in IT support and business operations tracks. Participants receive an educational stipend, which can count as household income for housing purposes and needs a benefits check.
requirements: Provider sets age and education eligibility
verify_note: Confirm age range, stipend amount and current Bay Area tracks with Year Up; stipend treatment must be reviewed with housing counsel.

name: Evening IT and Cloud Bootcamp (illustrative)
description: Part-time evening and weekend bootcamp covering IT fundamentals, cloud support and AWS cloud practitioner basics, for working adults who cannot leave their day job. Paid tuition with milestone payments; not on the state Eligible Training Provider List, so WIOA vouchers cannot be used.
verify_note: Illustrative example for the demo, not a real provider; shows how a Career-tier grant pays tuition when no free option fits.

name: Network Technician Certificate (illustrative ETPL-listed)
description: Part-time daytime network technician certificate covering cabling, routers, switches and CompTIA Network+ preparation. Listed on the California Eligible Training Provider List, so an eligible resident can use a WIOA Individual Training Account through a job center, with the grant paying only what is left.
requirements: WIOA eligibility determined by the job center
verify_note: Illustrative example for the demo, not a real provider; shows the WIOA-first funding order.

name: Data Center Technician Pathway (illustrative)
provider: Illustrative community college and employer partnership
description: Evening pathway into data center operations: server hardware, cabling, power and cooling basics, safety, and ticketing, with an employer interview at the end. An adjacent role to IT support that is growing with AI infrastructure.
requirements: Able to lift equipment; provider sets eligibility
verify_note: Illustrative example for the demo; validate employer demand before each cohort.

name: Full-Stack Coding Bootcamp with Income Share (illustrative, not approved)
description: Full-time daytime coding bootcamp financed through an income-share agreement. Shown so the app can explain why programs with income-share agreements or required loans are not approved for Bridgeline grants.
verify_note: Illustrative example of a program the grant rules reject (income-share agreement, no published outcomes).
